Claude Opus 4 is Anthropic's most capable and intelligent model, excelling in advanced coding, agentic search, and creative writing. It features a 200K context window, hybrid reasoning (instant or extended thinking), and industry-leading performance on SWE-bench and agentic tasks. Opus 4 is available via Anthropic API, Amazon Bedrock, and Google Cloud Vertex AI.

Where Anthropic says it does best

Anthropic describes Fable 5.2 as built "for demanding reasoning and long-horizon agentic work." Its examples are agent sessions that run for hours, multistep deep research, and analysis carried through to a finished document, spreadsheet or deck. Source: Claude Fable 5.2 overview, Choosing the right model
Where Anthropic says it does best

Anthropic recommends Opus 5.5 as the starting model for most workloads, and Fable 5.2 when Opus 5.5 evals at xhigh or max effort still fall short. Source: Choosing the right model, What's new in Claude Fable 5.2
Where Anthropic says it does best

Coding: the launch post reports FrontierCode 2.0 at 49.1% (Opus 5.5: 45.5%) and FrontierSWE v2 at 69.9% (Opus 5.5: 62.3%). At high effort it scores about level with Opus 5.5 on FrontierCode at roughly half the cost per task. Anthropic ran or reported these figures itself. Source: Introducing Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2
Where Anthropic says it does best

Agentic and computer-use work: the launch post reports Remote Labor Index 41.3% (Opus 5.5: 21.3%), OSWorld 2.1 89.3% (Opus 5.5: 87.2%) and Terminal-Bench-Science 74.6% (Opus 5.5: 58.7%). Source: Introducing Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2
Where Anthropic says it does best

Science, mathematics and hardware: Anthropic reports Humanity's Last Exam with tools at 74.2% (Opus 5.5: 67.7%), a formalization of Fermat's Last Theorem by about 1,000 Fable 5.2 agents in 30 hours, and three electronic devices designed through to boards ready for manufacture. The prompting guide names scientific discovery and mathematics as the work where max effort makes most sense. Source: Introducing Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2, Prompting Claude Fable 5.2
Where Anthropic says it does best

Long unattended runs and orchestration: the prompting guide says Fable 5.2 "works well on long-running asynchronous tasks," and early testers had good results using it to plan for and direct other models. Source: Prompting Claude Fable 5.2
